title: 2 Samuel Chapter 23 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Samuel chapter 23 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 23 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Samuel Chapter 23.

questions.question: Who is described as 'the sweet psalmist of Israel' in 2 Samuel 23?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:1 identifies David as 'the sweet psalmist of Israel.'

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 23, by whom did the Spirit speak?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:2 states that the Spirit of the LORD spoke by David.

questions.question: What must a ruler be, according to the words spoken in 2 Samuel 23?
options: Just and ruling in the fear of God
questions.correctAnswer: Just and ruling in the fear of God
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:3 says 'He that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God.'

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 23, the ruler is compared to what natural phenomenon?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:4 compares the ruler to 'the light of the morning, when the sun riseth, even a morning without clouds.'

questions.question: True or False: David says God made with him an everlasting covenant, sure in all things.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:5 states that God made with David an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things and sure.

questions.question: Who are described as 'sons of Belial' in 2 Samuel 23?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:6 calls the sons of Belial as those who are like thorns to be thrust away, implying they are wicked.

questions.question: True or False: The sons of Belial can easily be taken with hands.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:6 says the sons of Belial 'cannot be taken with hands.'

questions.question: What must a man have if he touches the sons of Belial according to 2 Samuel 23?
options: Iron and the staff of a spear
questions.correctAnswer: Iron and the staff of a spear
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:7 says the man that touches them must be fenced with iron and the staff of a spear.

questions.question: Who is the mighty man that slew eight hundred men at one time?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:8 identifies Adino the Eznite as the man who lifted his spear against eight hundred whom he slew at one time.

questions.question: True or False: Eleazar the son of Dodo was one of the three mighty men with David.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:9 states Eleazar was one of the three mighty men with David.

questions.question: What happened to Eleazar's hand when he fought the Philistines?
options: His hand clave unto the sword
His hand was pierced by a spear
His hand was burned by fire
questions.correctAnswer: His hand clave unto the sword
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:10 says Eleazar's hand clave unto the sword because he smote the Philistines until his hand was weary.

questions.question: Where was the piece of ground full of lentiles that Shammah defended?
options: In the midst of the battlefield
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:11-12 describes that the Philistines were gathered into a troop where there was a piece of ground full of lentiles, which Shammah defended.

questions.question: What did the LORD do when Shammah defended the lentiles?
options: He sent a plague on the Philistines
He made the sun stand still
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:12 says 'the LORD wrought a great victory' when Shammah defended the lentiles.

questions.question: Who were the three that went to David in the harvest time to the cave of Adullam?
options: Three of the sons of Belial
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:13 says three of the thirty chief went to David in the harvest time unto the cave of Adullam.

questions.question: True or False: The garrison of the Philistines was in Bethlehem when David was in an hold.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:14 states that David was in an hold and the garrison of the Philistines was in Bethlehem.

medium.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 23 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Samuel Chapter 23 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was David's reaction when his three mighty men brought him water from the well of Bethlehem?
options: He poured it out to the LORD and refused to drink it.
He gave it to his soldiers.
questions.correctAnswer: He poured it out to the LORD and refused to drink it.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:16-17 explains that David would not drink the water because he considered it the blood of the men who risked their lives, so he poured it out as an offering to the LORD.

questions.question: Who was chief among the three mighty men and lifted his spear against three hundred, gaining a name among them?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:18 states that Abishai, brother of Joab, was chief among the three and lifted his spear against three hundred, earning a name among them.

questions.question: How does David's refusal to drink the water from Bethlehem demonstrate biblical integrity?
options: He showed selfishness by not drinking.
He honored the sacrifice of his men by not taking their risk lightly.
He ignored the needs of his body.
He disrespected his men by rejecting their gift.
questions.correctAnswer: He honored the sacrifice of his men by not taking their risk lightly.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:16-17 shows David's respect for the risk his men took and his unwillingness to treat their sacrifice lightly, demonstrating integrity and honor.

questions.question: What notable action did Benaiah son of Jehoiada perform according to 2 Samuel 23?
options: He slew two lionlike men of Moab and a lion in a pit during snow.
He was chief among the three mighty men.
He defended a field of lentils from the Philistines.
He brought water to David from Bethlehem.
questions.correctAnswer: He slew two lionlike men of Moab and a lion in a pit during snow.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:20 describes Benaiah's valorous acts, including slaying two lionlike men of Moab and a lion in a pit during the snow.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Samuel 23, David was willing to drink the water brought by the three mighty men because it was a precious gift.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:16-17 clearly explains that David refused to drink the water to honor the lives risked by his men, considering it as their blood, so he poured it out instead.

questions.question: Which virtue is exemplified by David pouring out the water to the LORD rather than drinking it himself?
questions.explanation: David's act of pouring out the water to the LORD (2 Samuel 23:16-17) expresses humility and reverence by honoring God and the sacrifice of his men rather than satisfying his own desire.

questions.question: Who was described as the most honorable of the three mighty men but did not attain to the first three?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:19 says Abishai was the most honorable of the three so he was their captain, but he did not attain to the first three mighty men.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about faith through the example of David longing for water from Bethlehem?
options: Faith includes trusting God's timing and honoring sacrifices.
Faith means fulfilling all personal desires immediately.
Faith ignores the risks others take.
Faith is only about physical needs.
questions.correctAnswer: Faith includes trusting God's timing and honoring sacrifices.
questions.explanation: David's longing for water (2 Samuel 23:15) and subsequent refusal to drink it (vv.16-17) teach trusting God's timing and honoring the sacrifices made by others in faith.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the character trait demonstrated by Benaiah when he killed the Egyptian with his own spear?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:21 describes Benaiah’s courage and resourcefulness when he disarmed the Egyptian and killed him with his own spear.

questions.question: True or False: Abishai was set over the guard by David because he was more honorable than the thirty mighty men.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:23 says Benaiah, not Abishai, was more honorable than the thirty and was set over the guard by David.

questions.question: How does the story of the three mighty men bringing water to David teach about generosity and sacrifice?
options: It shows willingness to risk life for others’ needs.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows willingness to risk life for others’ needs.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:14-16 illustrates the three men's willingness to break through enemy lines and risk their lives to fulfill David's desire, modeling generous sacrifice.

questions.question: Who among David’s mighty men is noted for slaying three hundred men with his spear?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:18 states Abishai lifted his spear against three hundred and slew them, earning a name among the three mighty men.

questions.question: Which lesson about leadership is illustrated in 2 Samuel 23:3-4 and reflected in the conduct of David’s mighty men?
options: Leaders must be just and fear God, shining as a cloudless morning light.
Leaders should seek personal glory above all.
Leadership is about strict control without compassion.
Might alone defines a leader’s success.
questions.correctAnswer: Leaders must be just and fear God, shining as a cloudless morning light.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:3-4 teaches that ruling men requires justice and fear of God, like the bright morning light, a principle reflected by David’s righteous leadership and his mighty men’s loyalty.

questions.question: True or False: The three mighty men brought water to David from a well located inside the Philistine camp.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:16 specifies the water was drawn from the well of Bethlehem by the gate, outside the Philistine camp which was in the valley of Rephaim.

questions.question: What can believers learn about prayer and desire from David’s longing for water in 2 Samuel 23:15?
options: It shows that honest expression of desire is part of faith.
It teaches that desires should never be spoken aloud.
It discourages longing for physical needs.
It indicates God ignores human desires.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that honest expression of desire is part of faith.
questions.explanation: David’s longing in 2 Samuel 23:15 demonstrates how expressing honest desires can be part of a believer’s trust and faith before God.

hard.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 23 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Samuel Chapter 23.

questions.question: Who was the armourbearer to Joab, son of Zeruiah, mentioned among David's mighty men?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 Samuel 23:37 identifies Naharai the Beerothite as the armourbearer to Joab, son of Zeruiah.

questions.question: Which two mighty men mentioned in this chapter share a common tribal affiliation as Ithrites?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:38 notes that Ira and Gareb are both Ithrites, indicating their tribal affiliation.

questions.question: What reason did David give for not drinking the water brought to him from the well of Bethlehem?
options: It was holy water reserved for the LORD
It was the blood of the men who risked their lives
He was thirsty but wanted to honor a vow
questions.correctAnswer: It was the blood of the men who risked their lives
questions.explanation: According to 2 Samuel 23:17, David refused to drink the water as it represented the blood of the men who risked their lives to get it.

questions.question: Which of David's mighty men killed two lionlike men of Moab and also slew a lion in a pit during snow time?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:20 describes Benaiah's exploits killing two lionlike men of Moab and a lion in a pit during snow.

questions.question: Which literary device is exemplified by the listing of David’s mighty men with their tribal and familial affiliations in this chapter?
questions.explanation: The chapter opens and closes with references to David’s authority and his mighty men, creating an inclusio framing the text (2 Samuel 23:1 and 23:39).

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew term 'sons of Belial' as used in this chapter?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew phrase 'sons of Belial' in 2 Samuel 23:6 refers to morally corrupt or worthless men, a common Old Testament expression.

questions.question: Which mighty man is described as lifting his spear against 800 men and slaying them at one time?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:8 states that Adino the Eznite lifted up his spear against eight hundred men and slew them in one encounter.

questions.question: Which passage in the New Testament echoes the theme of the 'anointed of the God of Jacob' mentioned in 2 Samuel 23:1?
questions.explanation: Acts 10:38 refers to Jesus being anointed by God with the Holy Spirit and power, echoing the messianic theme introduced in 2 Samuel 23:1.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 23:4, the ruler who is just is compared to what natural phenomenon?
options: The light of the morning without clouds
questions.correctAnswer: The light of the morning without clouds
questions.explanation: Verse 4 compares a just ruler to the light of the morning when the sun rises without clouds, symbolizing clarity and hope.

questions.question: Which two mighty men are described as 'most honourable of three' but did not attain to the first three?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:19 and 23:23 describe Abishai and Benaiah as most honourable among the three but not equaling the first three mighty men.

questions.question: True or False: David was willing to drink the water brought from Bethlehem by his three mighty men as a sign of his victory.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:16-17 shows David refused to drink the water because it symbolized the blood of the men who risked their lives.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage shares a similar theme with 2 Samuel 23:3 about ruling justly and in the fear of God?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:12 emphasizes that kings who do not execute justice are wicked, paralleling 2 Samuel 23:3's teaching on just rulership.

questions.question: Who was the brother of Joab mentioned as chief among the three mighty men?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:18 identifies Abishai, brother of Joab, as chief among the three mighty men.

questions.question: Which geographical location is mentioned as the birthplace or origin of Elhanan, one of David’s mighty men?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:24 names Elhanan as the son of Dodo of Bethlehem, indicating his origin.

questions.question: True or False: The phrase 'sweet psalmist of Israel' in 2 Samuel 23:1 refers to David's role as a songwriter and musician.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:1 calls David the 'sweet psalmist of Israel,' highlighting his recognized role as a composer of psalms and songs.

theological.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 23 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Samuel Chapter 23 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 23:3, what is a defining characteristic of one who rules over men?
options: He must be just, ruling in the fear of God
He must be wealthy and influential
He must be strong and fearless
He must be wise and cunning
questions.correctAnswer: He must be just, ruling in the fear of God
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:3 states that 'He that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God,' emphasizing justice and reverence for God as essential qualities for leadership.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 23:4 use as a metaphor for a just ruler?
options: The light of the morning without clouds
A mighty lion in the forest
questions.correctAnswer: The light of the morning without clouds
questions.explanation: Verse 4 compares a just ruler to 'the light of the morning, when the sun riseth, even a morning without clouds,' symbolizing clarity, hope, and blessing that come with righteous leadership.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is expressed in 2 Samuel 23:5 regarding God's relationship with David's house?
options: The doctrine of the everlasting covenant
The doctrine of justification by faith
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of the everlasting covenant
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:5 speaks of God making 'an everlasting covenant' with David, which is foundational for the doctrine of God's unchanging promises and covenant faithfulness (see also Jeremiah 33:20-21).

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 23:6-7, what is the fate of the sons of Belial described as?
options: They are like thorns that must be burned with fire
They will be exalted and honored
They will inherit the land of Israel
They will become leaders among men
questions.correctAnswer: They are like thorns that must be burned with fire
questions.explanation: Verses 6-7 portray the sons of Belial as 'thorns thrust away' who require iron and fire to be overcome, symbolizing the inevitability of divine judgment against wickedness.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted in 2 Samuel 23:2 where it says, 'The Spirit of the LORD spake by me'?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 23:2 emphasizes that the Spirit of the LORD inspired David's words, revealing God's sovereign control over revelation and prophecy (cf. 2 Peter 1:21).

questions.question: How do 2 Samuel 23:8 and 23:10 illustrate the theme of divine empowerment in battle?
options: David's mighty men achieved victories through the LORD's help
The men fought relying solely on their own strength
They used clever tactics to outsmart their enemies
They hired mercenaries to win battles
questions.correctAnswer: David's mighty men achieved victories through the LORD's help
questions.explanation: Verses 8 and 10 recount how mighty men like Adino and Eleazar slew many foes, with verse 10 explicitly stating 'the LORD wrought a great victory that day,' demonstrating divine empowerment in human warfare.

questions.question: What does the act of David refusing to drink the water brought by his three mighty men in 2 Samuel 23:16-17 symbolize doctrinally?
options: Respect for the sacrificial risk of others' lives
A sign of distrust toward his men
questions.correctAnswer: Respect for the sacrificial risk of others' lives
questions.explanation: David's refusal to drink the water 'because it was the blood of the men that went in jeopardy of their lives' (verse 17) symbolizes honoring the costly sacrifice of others and sanctifying their risk before God.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 23:20-21, what extraordinary acts did Benaiah perform, illustrating what doctrine about God's provision for His servants?
options: He slew two lion-like men and an Egyptian, showing God's protection and strength given to His servants
He built great fortresses, showing God's blessing on human effort
He prophesied victory, showing God's foreknowledge
He administered justice, showing God's lawfulness
questions.correctAnswer: He slew two lion-like men and an Egyptian, showing God's protection and strength given to His servants
questions.explanation: Verses 20-21 recount Benaiah's mighty deeds against formidable foes, illustrating the doctrine that God equips and protects His faithful servants to triumph over enemies (cf. Psalm 18:34).

questions.question: What combined teaching do 2 Samuel 23:3 and 2 Samuel 23:5 convey about God's ideal king and covenant?
options: God's ideal king rules justly in fear of God and is established by an everlasting covenant
God's ideal king must be a warrior and conquer lands
God's ideal king should amass wealth and power
God's ideal king rules by human wisdom alone
questions.correctAnswer: God's ideal king rules justly in fear of God and is established by an everlasting covenant
questions.explanation: Verse 3 highlights just rule in the fear of God, and verse 5 affirms God's everlasting covenant with David, together teaching that divine kingship combines justice, reverence, and covenantal promise.

questions.question: How do 2 Samuel 23:6-7 and 2 Samuel 23:13-14 together illustrate God's justice and providence in the midst of conflict?
options: God judges the wicked severely and protects His servant David during enemy siege
God allows the wicked to prosper and abandons David
God condemns all human warfare as evil
questions.correctAnswer: God judges the wicked severely and protects His servant David during enemy siege
questions.explanation: Verses 6-7 describe the severe judgment on the sons of Belial, while verses 13-14 place David protected in a stronghold during the Philistine siege, showing God's justice and providential care.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 23:1 reveal about David's identity and role in redemptive history?
options: David is the anointed of God and the sweet psalmist of Israel
David is merely a warrior king without spiritual significance
David is a prophet who rejected kingship
David is an outsider to God's covenant people
questions.correctAnswer: David is the anointed of God and the sweet psalmist of Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 1 introduces David as 'the anointed of the God of Jacob' and 'sweet psalmist,' highlighting his messianic and worship roles, foreshadowing Christ and Israel’s spiritual heritage.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about human sinfulness and divine justice is taught by the description of the sons of Belial in 2 Samuel 23:6-7?
options: Wickedness results in inevitable, thorough judgment by God
Sin is not serious if hidden
questions.correctAnswer: Wickedness results in inevitable, thorough judgment by God
questions.explanation: The sons of Belial are portrayed as thorns that must be burned with fire, symbolizing God's certain and complete judgment on sin and evil (2 Samuel 23:6-7).

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 23:23 indicate about Benaiah's role among David's men?
options: He was more honorable than the thirty but not among the first three, and was set over David’s guard
He was the king’s chief advisor
questions.correctAnswer: He was more honorable than the thirty but not among the first three, and was set over David’s guard
questions.explanation: Verse 23 explicitly states Benaiah's distinguished honor and his appointment over David’s personal guard, illustrating God's order and gifting in leadership roles.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 2 Samuel 23 glorifies human violence and warfare. What does 2 Samuel 23:10-12 actually teach about God's role in victory?
options: God is the one who wrought a great victory, enabling human agents
Victory is purely due to human strength
God condemns all warfare without exception
questions.correctAnswer: God is the one who wrought a great victory, enabling human agents
questions.explanation: Verses 10-12 narrate how the LORD wrought a great victory through David’s mighty men, showing divine sovereign involvement rather than mere human valor, affirming God’s providence in conflict.

questions.question: How does the list of David’s mighty men in 2 Samuel 23:24-39 contribute to biblical theology regarding community and service?
options: It shows a diverse group united under God’s king, emphasizing faithful service and communal strength
It glorifies only the top three men
It highlights social divisions in Israel
It focuses on wealth and status
questions.correctAnswer: It shows a diverse group united under God’s king, emphasizing faithful service and communal strength
questions.explanation: The extensive list reflects varied backgrounds united in loyal service to David, underscoring biblical themes of unity, diversity, and faithful ministry under God’s anointed ruler.
